title: Depth two for a finite local dual
statement:
theorem dual_depth_ge_two (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hR : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ depth (R := R) R) :
    (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ depth (R := R) (Module.Dual R N)

proof.text: Extract a length at least two regular sequence from the depth supremum and take its first two elements x,y in the maximal ideal.

Multiplication by x is injective on Hom(N,R) pointwise. If y*f belongs to x Hom(N,R), regularity of y modulo x forces all f(n) into xR. Invert the injective multiplication-by-x equivalence R to xR, corestrict f and compose with the inverse. This produces a linear quotient f prime and proves y regular modulo x on the dual.

The dual is finite by Noetherianity. If nonzero, Nakayama converts the weakly regular pair in the maximal ideal into a regular sequence, so its length bounds depth below. If the dual is zero, its depth is infinity by the definition.
